label: Monado MOC
title: Monado MOC (Samsung Odyssey+)
intro: The MOC calibration recordings of the Monado SLAM Datasets, made with a Samsung Odyssey+ headset: its two tracking cameras and its IMU, 4 camera-only and 4 camera + IMU recordings.
reading: Runs. We ran MVIS 0.4.1 (development version of 2026-11-26) on all 8 recordings, and Kalibr and Basalt on the 4 camera-only recordings, on 2026-11-27. The camera + IMU solves of Kalibr and Basalt are from October 2026. That Kalibr run uses its scale-misalignment IMU model, with a change that starts its spline from both cameras.

Chart centre. Each chart is centred on the Monado authors' own Basalt calibration of this headset, made from one recording: extras/calibration.raw.json for the camera–IMU distance, baseline and time offset, and its kb4 version (calibration.kb4.json) for the intrinsics. Their IMU terms are not used: the released recordings appear to carry the authors' IMU correction already, so those charts, and t_ga, are centred on the MVIS median.
no_repeatability: This study has no repeatability cells: they are computed for the leaderboard batch only, and 4 recordings are too few for the test. Each tool's spread is in Parameters by sensor.
study_note: Separate study (batch 2026-11-27): MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt on the 4 MOC camera-only and 4 camera + IMU recordings, run outside the leaderboard batch, so it has no row here.

families.title: cam0 + cam1 stereo
families.read_first: Each tool calibrates both cameras and their baseline from the images alone, on the 4 camcalib recordings.
notes: Every tool ran on the same 4 recordings, each with its own camera model: MVIS equidistant, Kalibr pinhole-equi and Basalt kb4, the same polynomial.

families.title: cam0 + cam1 + IMU
families.read_first: MVIS starts from its camera-only result of the same round and refines the intrinsics. Kalibr's intrinsics and baselines are inputs from its own camera calibration on the same camera + IMU recording; its td, lever and IMU intrinsics are solved given them.

poor.text: On MOC05, MOC08 and MOC11 Kalibr's own camera calibration is off: fx 296–301 px, against about 270 px from MVIS on the same recordings. On MOC05 its accelerometer scale also reaches 93 on z.

notes: Every tool ran on the same 4 recordings, each with its own camera model: MVIS equidistant, Kalibr pinhole-equi and Basalt pinhole-radtan8 (the dataset authors' model, so its intrinsics are shown, not compared).
MVIS starts from its camera-only result of the same round and refines the intrinsics; Kalibr's and Basalt's cameras come from their own camera stage on the same recording.
pinhole-radtan8, the dataset authors' model; its intrinsics are shown only.
